item.title: Galaxy cluster thermodynamics at z=1.7: Resolved tSZ and X-ray analysis of CL J0459.6-4946
item.description: arXiv:2611.00132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Measurements of the entropy and temperature distribution of the intracluster medium (ICM) of local clusters have proven pivotal for the study of cluster astrophysics. Here, we extend these measurements to $z=1.7$ with a resolved analysis of the ICM in ACT/SPT-CL J0459.6-4946. By combining high-resolution thermal Sunyaev-Zeldovich measurements using new, deep ALMA Band 1 and 3 observations, with archival X-ray data, we conclude that the cluster has (i) an ICM with a flat and relatively high ($\approx 200$ keV cm$^2$) entropy distribution out to $\approx 0.3\,r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$, (ii) a hot core ($T_{\mathrm{e}} \simeq 14$ keV) with a declining temperature profile, (iii) a short effective path length along the line of sight of $l_{\mathrm{eff}} \simeq (0.75 \pm 0.05) \times r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$, and (iv) a clumpiness factor $C = \langle n_{\mathrm{e}}^2 \rangle / \langle n_{\mathrm{e}} \rangle^2 \simeq 1.17 \pm 0.05$ within $r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$. Its dynamic nature and high redshift suggest that the cluster is still thermalising its ICM, consistent with a relatively large hydrostatic mass bias of $b = 1 - M_{500,\mathrm{c,HE}}/M_{500,\mathrm{c,WL}} = 0.27^{+0.32}_{-0.67}$ that we measure with respect to the weak lensing mass. Furthermore, a region with low entropy and high density to the south of the cluster centre is observed in the X-rays yet absent in the Compton-$y$ map, indicating pressure equilibrium; we interpret this as a sloshing cold front -- the first such detection at high redshifts. This case study demonstrates that $\approx 3$h-long ALMA observations, combined with comparatively "short" X-ray exposures ($\approx 122$ ks), can fully characterise the ICM at high redshift, opening a path towards the thermodynamics of young and distant galaxy clusters for larger samples.

item.title: Developing Environments: Formation and Quenching at Cosmic Noon Traced by the Large-scale Distribution of Gas and Galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2611.00190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Environmental density correlates with galaxy properties in the local Universe, but how and when these trends emerge is unclear: at cosmic noon, large-scale structures are still assembling and galaxies quench rapidly for debated reasons. We study how the formation and quenching histories of massive galaxies at $1.7<z<3.5$ depend on environment, using two independent tracers: galaxy number density ($\delta_\#$) from COSMOS-Web and intergalactic neutral hydrogen ($\delta_{HI}$, cool gas) from LATIS Ly$\alpha$ tomography. We combine 139 Blue Jay JWST/NIRSpec galaxies with 57 DAWN JWST Archive prism spectra in COSMOS, deriving stellar masses, star formation histories, dust attenuation, and Na\,{\sc d} outflow rates from joint spectro-photometric \texttt{Prospector} fits. In massive quiescent galaxies, the formation-to-quenching interval increases with density. AGN and Na\,{\sc d} outflows are confined to $\delta_\#<0.5$ and elevated Ly$\alpha$ absorption ($\delta_{HI}>1$), mostly in massive quiescent galaxies showing both. About 65\% of the sample follows a correlation between the tracers; two outlier regions stand out. A galaxy-rich, gas-poor region ($\delta_\#>2$, $\delta_{HI}<1$) coincides with one of the most massive Hyperion protocluster cores, where the gas is plausibly fully ionized; its quiescent galaxies formed earlier and lack significant AGN activity and outflows. A galaxy-poor, gas-rich region ($\delta_\#<1$, $\delta_{HI}>1$), within 60 cMpc of the densest Hyperion cores, hosts rapidly quenched galaxies with a high incidence of AGN and outflows. This \emph{developing environment}, distinct from both mature protoclusters and the field, likely traces massive halos still assembling. Galaxy counts alone cannot capture the environment at cosmic noon: jointly mapping galaxies and cool gas is crucial to understand how environment regulates gas accretion, star formation, and quenching.

item.title: EMBER: A Little Red Dot Candidate at $z_{\rm spec}=10.36$ in the Seed Black Hole Era
item.description: arXiv:2611.00195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Little red dots (LRDs) are a newly discovered population that may trace rapidly growing black holes (BHs) and provide a link between seed BHs and luminous active galactic nuclei (AGNs). However, no LRD had previously been spectroscopically confirmed at $z>10$, leaving this earliest phase observationally unexplored. Using JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy from the EMBER program, we measure a spectroscopic redshift of $z_{\rm spec}=10.361^{+0.003}_{-0.002}$ for \target, the highest-redshift LRD candidate known to date. The redshift is constrained by a prominent Ly$\alpha$ break and multiple tentative emission lines, including C\,{\sc iv}\,$\lambda\lambda1549,1551$ and [O\,{\sc iii}]\,$\lambda4363$ detected at $S/N=3.9$ and $3.6$, respectively. Its extreme NIRCam-MIRI color of $m_{\rm F444W}-m_{\rm F770W}=1.82\pm0.1$, characteristic V-shaped continuum with a turnover near the Balmer limit, and continuum slopes of $\beta_{\rm UV}=-2.26^{+0.11}_{-0.11}$ and $\beta_{\rm opt}=1.17^{+0.74}_{-0.70}$ all support its LRD nature. A possible iron complex at $\lambda_{\rm rest}\sim0.24$--$0.25\,{\rm \mu m}$ and a possibly high $\log\left([{\rm O\,III]\,\lambda4363/\rm H\gamma}\right)=0.17^{+0.24}_{-0.22}$ further support an AGN-like interpretation, as seen in previously known LRDs. Tentative detection of Ly$\alpha$ emission may indicate enhanced Ly$\alpha$ transmission at $z\sim10$. Our findings extend the observational frontier of BH growth into the seed-BH formation era, and upcoming MIRI spectroscopy will further establish the physical nature of the source.

item.title: MARTA: A "little" black hole hidden in a clumpy, metal-poor galaxy at z~3.8
item.description: arXiv:2611.00199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: JWST has extended the search for accreting black holes into the high-redshift, low-mass regime. We report a low-mass black hole candidate in MARTA 3887, a clumpy, metal-poor galaxy at $z=3.7694$, combining deep JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy, HST and JWST imaging, and archival VLT/MUSE data. We detect a broad H$\alpha$ component with $L_{\rm H\alpha,b}=2.35\times10^{41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and FWHM $=1270^{+260}_{-250}$ km s$^{-1}$, with no [O III] counterpart of comparable width. Under a broad-line-region interpretation, virial calibrations give $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=6.52^{+0.18}_{-0.23}$ and $\lambda_{\rm Edd}=0.07$, or up to 0.38 for alternative calibrations. The host comprises at least three compact clumps, with $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)=8.16^{+0.09}_{-0.10}$. If stellar photoionization dominates the narrow lines, the gas is highly ionized and metal poor, with $12+\log({\rm O/H})=7.68\pm0.04$ ($\simeq0.10\,Z_\odot$). The inferred $M_{\rm BH}/M_\star=2.3\%$ lies about 2 dex above the extrapolated local relation, suggesting that black-hole growth has outpaced the assembly of the observed host. If growth began only when the first 10% of the observed stellar mass had formed ($t_{10}=92$ Myr ago), a $10^2\,M_\odot$ seed would require a lifetime-mean Eddington ratio $\simeq5.7$; earlier growth or a more massive, e.g. direct-collapse, seed would allow sub-Eddington mean accretion. MUSE reveals extended Ly$\alpha$ emission ($\simeq6.5$-6.9 proper kpc), offset by $+64^{+10}_{-8}$ km s$^{-1}$ from systemic, with a provisional escape fraction of $\simeq0.44$. Together with a Mg II doublet ratio close to the optically thin limit and a high [O III]/[O II] ratio, this makes MARTA 3887 a laboratory to study black-hole growth, stellar assembly, and ionizing-photon escape jointly.

item.title: A Supermagnified Little Red Dot with a Resolved Host
item.description: arXiv:2611.00202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Little red dots (LRDs) are an intriguing new class of sources in the early universe discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) characterized by V-shaped spectra and extremely compact sizes. Their underlying mechanisms still remain the subject of ongoing debate. We present JWST observations of a gravitationally lensed LRD nicknamed "Best Friend" at $z_{\rm spec} = 8.297\pm0.002$. Its high magnification factor of $\mu = 36^{+8}_{-12}$ makes it the highest magnified LRD reported to date and unveils both the resolved structure of its host and a central engine less than 7 pc in size. The spectrum of the central engine, in which broad lines are not detected, possibly owing to the limited S/N and spectral resolution, is better interpreted as black hole activity rather than a dense star cluster. The latter cannot be fully excluded, but if true, the resulting lower limit on stellar density would be $>1.25^{+0.4}_{-0.3}\cdot10^6 \mathrm{M_{\odot}/pc}^2$, which is around 2 orders of magnitude higher than stellar densities of typical clusters at high-z. By performing a spatially resolved analysis of NIRCam photometry and NIRSpec/PRISM spectroscopy, we find that the host stellar mass is $\log(M_\star/M_{\odot}) = 7.3^{+0.2}_{-0.8}$. Best Friend demonstrates the power of lensing to reveal the morphologies of LRDs.

item.title: Dust-induced reversal of the optical wavelength dependence of spiral-arm pitch angles
item.description: arXiv:2611.00208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical density-wave scenario predicts a blue-to-red age--colour gradient across the spiral arms of disc galaxies as a consequence of shock-induced star formation. However, observations of spiral-arm pitch angles at different wavelengths sometimes suggest the opposite trend, namely a red-to-blue ``colour jump''. The origin of this apparent contradiction remains unclear. In this work, we investigate the effects of dust attenuation on post-shock stellar emission, together with the streamline motions of gas and stellar populations. We find that dust attenuation in regions with relatively high optical depths, $\hat{\tau}_{V} \gtrsim 0.2$, can produce an apparent red-to-blue spatial sequence, with respect to the shock location, by reversing the relative positions of the flux maxima of stellar populations observed in different bands. Moreover, streamline motions confine post-shock stellar populations near the spiral arms for longer than in a circular-orbit model, thereby modifying the spatial distribution of the emitted light. We conclude that the apparent red-to-blue colour jump does not necessarily contradict the classical density-wave scenario. Instead, it can arise from the same post-shock stellar populations that intrinsically produce a blue-to-red age--colour gradient if their emission is modified by dust attenuation.

item.title: The MAGPI Survey: the evolution of galaxy spin-filament alignments since z~0.3
item.description: arXiv:2611.00212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present measurements of galaxy spin-filament alignments at 0.20<z<0.42 using the MAGPI Survey, exploiting resolved stellar and ionised gas kinematics to reconstruct 3D spin axes. Cosmic filaments are identified using a stellar mass-matched constant-number-density population from the GAMA, MAGPI Redshift Survey and DESI datasets. We detect a flipping of the statistical alignment signal at z~0.3 as a function of M*: low-mass galaxies preferentially exhibit spins parallel to the direction of their host filaments, while high-mass galaxies tend towards perpendicular orientations. The transition mass is measured to be log(M{*,t}/Msun)~10.8, approximately 0.6 dex higher than the value for the SAMI Galaxy Survey at z~0.05. Bootstrap analysis gives 99.5% confidence that the transition mass is higher for MAGPI than SAMI. At fixed stellar mass MAGPI galaxies exhibit stronger parallel alignments than their SAMI counterparts, suggesting evolution of spin-filament alignments over the past ~3 Gyr. The gaseous component in MAGPI galaxies is more closely aligned with filaments than the stellar component, relative to a M*-matched SAMI sample. This indicates a stronger coupling between ionised gas and the large-scale structure at z~0.3, consistent with coherent gas accretion onto filaments remaining efficient at higher M*. At z~0 we detect a transition toward perpendicular alignments at lower M*, while the gas and stellar components exhibit similar alignments relative to filaments, likely due to the cumulative effects of mergers and secular evolution.

item.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). Mass-to-light ratio of elliptical galaxies: constraints from strong lensing
item.description: arXiv:2611.00224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mass is among the most fundamental properties describing a galaxy. The relation between the luminosity and the total mass of a galaxy contains information on the efficiency of the star formation process and on the distribution of dark matter. We used strong gravitational lensing data from the Euclid Quick Data Release 1 (Q1) to constrain the total mass enclosed within an aperture of $5\,h^{-1}$kpc, $M_5$, of elliptical galaxies. Our analysis is based on a sample of 95 lenses, which we built by ensuring that their selection function is reproducible. This enabled us to correct our inference for selection effects. The average $\log_{10}{(M_5\,h\,M_\odot^{-1})}$ for a galaxy with an $r$-band luminosity of $10^{10.7}L_{\odot}\,h^{-2}$ at $z=0.5$ is $11.30\pm0.02$. The mass $M_5$ scales with luminosity to the power $\beta_\mathrm{L}=0.71\pm0.07$, and decreases with increasing redshift at fixed luminosity. Assuming a scenario in which galaxies grow by mergers and stellar populations evolve passively, these correlations imply that $M_5$ increases with time for individual galaxies. These measurements provide a useful benchmark for testing models of galaxy structure and evolution that make predictions on the distribution of total mass on the scales of $5\,h^{-1}$kpc.

item.title: The L1157 filament as traced in HNCO by the LMT
item.description: arXiv:2611.00336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Context. The L1157 outflow is a prototype of chemically active outflows where to look for molecular species linked to complex chemistry. Aims. With the aim of imaging the large (parsec) scale structure of key prebiotic molecules, we have mapped the whole blue-lobe of the L1157 outflow with the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT), proving the potential of this facility to detect weak and extended molecular emission. Methods. Isocyanic acid, HNCO, an important precursor of complex chemistry, was chosen to be observed in its (4_0,4-3_0-3) transition at 87.925 GHz with the SEQUOIA focal-plane array, covering an area of 3x3 arcmin2 centered at the position of the main shock L1157-B1, which included a large portion of the vicinity of the protostellar region. Results. The HNCO emission was detected not only from the outflow but it also was found tracing a structure of about 0.3 pc in length, corresponding to the filament from which the protostellar system was born. Conclusions. The HNCO molecule was found to be a tracer of the densest part of filaments in molecular clouds, and given its importance in the formation of more complex molecules, its presence in the cold, quiescent filamentary gas indicates that the building blocks of complex chemistry are already well established in stages prior to protostellar warming or shocks. By allowing the detection of structures related with the filament, these observations proved the LMT potentialities to map weak and extended components in molecular clouds.

item.title: Modeling CO Line Luminosity with FIRE simulations: II. Comparison With Observations, CO Luminosity Functions and Redshift Evolution
item.description: arXiv:2611.00368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present predictions for the CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) luminosities of 765, 850, 887 and 915 galaxies at z=0, 1, 2 and 3, respectively, drawn from the Feedback in Realistic Environments (FIRE-2) simulations and post-processed with SKIRT radiative transfer and CLOUDY line emission calculations. We compare our CO line luminosity predictions with existing observations. At z=0, our predictions reproduce the observed scatter and mean relation between star formation rate (SFR) and CO(1-0) luminosity for both massive star-forming galaxies and low-metallicity dwarf galaxies. We also reproduce the observed superlinear power-law slope between CO(1-0) luminosity and metallicity. At z=1, our CO(2-1) predictions scatter to much lower luminosities than observed, which likely reflects the limited sensitivity of current surveys. At fixed SFR, our CO(1-0) luminosities decrease by roughly an order of magnitude per unit increase in redshift. This decline is likely driven by the decrease in metallicity with increasing redshift, since FIRE-2 galaxies with comparable SFR and metallicity produce similar CO(1-0) luminosities regardless of redshift. At fixed stellar mass, the predicted luminosities show no redshift dependence. These results show that our FIRE-2 predictions reproduce the observed scaling relations between CO(1-0) luminosity and galaxy properties wherever the observed galaxies are robustly detected. This gives us confidence in our predictions for the regime where no observational data exist, and suggests that our luminosity predictions can be used to build predictive models for CO line intensity mapping experiments.

item.title: EMU/GAMA: Understanding the link between dust geometry and star formation rate in galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2611.00741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the link between dust obscuration and star formation rate (SFR) estimators using Halpha luminosities, L_Halpha and radio luminosities, L_radio. While the Balmer Decrement (BD) is the standard tool for attenuating Halpha, it can fail to account for optically thick dust regions from which Halpha cannot escape. The ratio of SFRs estimated from radio luminosity and L_Halpha corrected for dust attenuation using the BD can be used as a probe of the degree of optically thick dust affecting Halpha. We explore this combining Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) Early Science data at 887.5MHz in the Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA) G23 field with the GAMA data. We draw on dust estimates using both the BD and the dust mass, M_d, demonstrating systematic underlying dependencies with L_radio/L_Halpha. By combining the BD and M_d, we quantify how they relate to L_radio/L_Halpha and other galaxy properties. We use this approach to establish an Halpha SFR (SFR_Halpha) estimator that accounts for optically thick dust, demonstrating its consistency with conventional SFR indicators. Rather than proposing a replacement for standard correction methods, we aim to demonstrate the effectiveness of a dust geometry model that integrates both BD and M_d parameters. This H_dust parameter provides a more physically complete representation of optically thick environments that traditional methods may overlook, and can produce SFR estimates consistent with traditional techniques.

item.title: Introducing Aurora: A New Black Hole Seeding Model With Explicit Environmental Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.01315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Aurora, a black hole seeding module for the Mimic semi-analytic framework, in which the seed mass of each newly resolved halo is set by its environment. Motivated by evidence that early quiescent galaxies and overmassive black holes assemble in dense environments, Aurora replaces the fixed seed masses of conventional prescriptions with a continuous spectrum, coupling the seed mass to two environmental parameters, the local overdensity and the radial skewness of the surrounding haloes, and to the halo mass at seeding. Requiring only halo masses and positions, it applies to dark-matter-only simulations. Calibrated against Sage on the Millennium merger trees, this prescription leaves a lasting signal. Massive black holes are assembled from the seeds of many progenitors, seeds supplying 29 per cent of all black hole mass formed by $z=0$. A seed-dominated growth pathway, distinct from the accretion-dominated majority, emerges among galaxies assembled rapidly in dense, asymmetric environments. Environment-dependent seeding raises the quiescent fraction of seeded galaxies in massive haloes at $z \simeq 3.1$ by up to 70 per cent, with the excess concentrated in overdense environments, and a deficit in voids. Scrambling the seeding environments while preserving the mass spectrum erases this gradient. The two environmental couplings imprint separable signatures, broadening the scatter of the galaxy-black hole mass relation while preserving the stellar-halo mass relation and other Sage summary statistics. We discuss applying Aurora at gigaparsec scales and higher resolution, to understand the origins of massive black hole systems in contemporary deep surveys.

item.title: Witnessing pre-processing at intermediate redshift: observational evidence of infalling groups onto a merging galaxy cluster
item.description: arXiv:2611.01344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fraction of quenched galaxies increases with local density, and part of this trend is thought to arise in groups before cluster accretion (pre-processing). In merging clusters, this is difficult to separate from star formation triggered or suppressed by the cluster merger itself. We investigate whether five high-velocity galaxies in the merging cluster SPT-CL~J0307-6225 ($z=0.579$), distributed in two candidate infalling groups, show signs of group-scale environmental processing prior to accretion. We combine MUSE integral-field spectroscopy and HST imaging to derive [\ion{O}{ii}] kinematic maps, spectral classes, and star-formation rates (SFR), to understand the properties of the galaxies. We further use the Magneticum simulations and the phase-space information to determine if these galaxies are part of two groups, and if they will be accreted onto the merging cluster. Group~1 is a morphologically disturbed interacting pair bound to the cluster, with at least one galaxy classified as dusty starburst. Group~2 is a compact triplet at $\sim$4$\sigma_v$ from the cluster, in which two galaxies share a common [\ion{O}{ii}] envelope and the dominant member, an e(b) starburst, shows an elevated ionised-gas velocity dispersion. The SFR of both starburst galaxies lie within the scatter of the field star-forming main sequence, as expected for modest, interaction-triggered bursts. Close pairs at the phase-space position of group~2 occur for $\sim$1\% of comparable-mass cluster galaxies in Magneticum, so it is not unlikely for the group to be bound. Both groups show spatially resolved signatures of galaxy--galaxy interactions alongside ongoing star formation, supporting a pre-processing scenario in the environment of a merging cluster. Such group-scale interactions may contribute to the enhanced star formation reported in merging clusters.

item.title: Dynamically defined bulges reveal that early-type galaxies with compact bulges host more massive black holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}$ relation for early-type galaxies by introducing a uniform bulge defined by dynamical decomposition. From the set of nearby galaxies with accurately measured black hole masses, we select 30 early-type galaxies that have been observed with wide-field integral-field unit instruments (MUSE, ATLAS3D, or PPAK). For each galaxy, we construct an orbit-superposition Schwarzschild model and obtain its stellar orbit distribution. In this framework, we define the bulge uniformly as comprising stellar orbits with circularity $\lambda_z < 0.7$ (or, in an alternative definition, $\lambda_z < 0.2$) and lying within $r < 3$ kpc. From these orbits, we reconstruct the spatial density distribution of the bulge and measure its mass ($M_{bulge}$), size ($R_{bulge}$) and surface density slope ($\gamma_{bulge}$). We find that the dynamical bulge defined by $\lambda_z < 0.7$ yields masses that are systematically consistent with the photometric bulge masses. Comparing to the bulge from photometric decomposition, using this dynamical bulge definition slightly decreases the scatter around the best-fitting from 0.56 to 0.47. More interestingly, we identify a clear trend: at a given bulge mass, galaxies hosting more compact bulges (i.e. smaller bulge sizes or steeper bulge density slopes) systematically contain more massive black holes; eight outliers show overmassive BHs together with ultra-compact bulges. We interpret this as direct observational evidence that the $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}$ relation evolves over a galaxy's merger history, with that history imprinted in bulge compactness. Incorporating compactness via an $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}-R_{e, bulge}$ (or $\gamma_{bulge}$) relation brings the outliers into agreement and reduces the overall scatter of the sample to $\sim 0.3$.

item.title: Physically Motivated Stellar Populations for Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn with a Temperature-Dependent IMF
item.description: arXiv:2611.01595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The first few years of James Webb Space Telescope observations have identified previously undetected galaxies at $z>12$ and provided new constraints on galaxies at $z>8$. Many of these objects have stellar masses that are difficult to reconcile with $\Lambda$CDM, inferred from models not calibrated for the high-redshift Universe. This necessitates new, more astrophysically plausible stellar population models for estimating stellar masses of galaxies at cosmic dawn. We introduce a simple stellar population (SSP) library, Simple Stellar Populations with Temperature (SSPT), computed using a temperature-dependent stellar initial mass function and its implementation in the public code CIGALE. When used in a configuration designed for high-redshift galaxies that requires young stellar population ages, the new models predict stellar masses that are ~0.3-0.5 dex lower than estimates from similar CIGALE analyses using models calibrated to the local Universe, and nearly 2 dex lower than estimates from analyses using other codes and softer constraints on stellar ages. Application of these physically motivated stellar populations suggests that stellar masses of early star-forming galaxies are not in tension with $\Lambda$CDM, and that galaxy formation from virialized halos remains a reasonable hypothesis at the highest redshifts. The SSPT SSPs and their CIGALE implementation are released publicly.

item.title: An Unusually Clumpy Ultra-Diffuse Galaxy in the Coma Cluster: A Missing Link for Globular Cluster Formation?
item.description: arXiv:2611.01653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a study of Coma-B122, an unusually clumpy star-forming ultra-diffuse galaxy (UDG) in the Coma cluster outskirts, using deep Keck Cosmic Web Imager integral-field spectroscopy and Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam imaging. B122 hosts $\sim10$ luminous star-forming clumps contributing $\sim25$% of its luminosity and $\sim7$% of its stellar mass, with typical clump masses of $\sim10^6\ M_\odot$ comparable to the most massive super star clusters known in nearby starbursting dwarfs. The clumps form a distinctive ring configuration $\sim2$ kpc from the center. Full-spectrum fitting shows that $\sim12.5$% of the diffuse body's stellar mass formed during an extended episode of enhanced star formation over the past $\sim300$ Myr, within which all the clumps assembled. B122 shows evidence of weak ram-pressure stripping (RPS), including a diffuse light distribution truncated on the side facing the Coma center and extended to the opposite side, along with an asymmetric H I velocity profile. Its ordered stellar and ionized-gas rotation, cold gas fraction, and phase-space position are consistent with an early stage of infall. Spatial variations in clump star formation histories and gas-phase abundances further indicate that RPS-driven metal-poor gas inflow may have triggered and sustained the recent star formation. B122 may offer a rare present-day view of how UDGs assemble their globular cluster (GC) systems during cluster infall, although it remains uncertain if the clumps could survive as GCs. Future observations with higher spatial resolution and of more analogs are important to provide a complete picture of the formation and evolution of clumpy low-surface-brightness dwarf galaxies.

item.title: Simulating winds in the Galactic centre. II. Observational biases on HI clouds and a multi-wavelength comparison
item.description: arXiv:2611.02144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-velocity neutral hydrogen (HI) clouds found up to several kiloparsecs above the Galactic centre (GC) provide some of the most direct evidence for a nuclear wind in the Milky Way, yet the properties inferred for these clouds are influenced by how they are observed. Starting from a magnetohydrodynamical simulation in which supernova feedback drives a multiphase nuclear outflow, we generate mock HI observations matched to the angular resolution and sensitivity of Green Bank Telescope (GBT) surveys of the GC and analyse them in the same way as the real data. We find that observational effects substantially reshape the cloud population: beam smearing makes clouds appear larger, rounder and more diffuse, while noise erases faint clouds and strips low-density gas from the others. These effects combined, together with confusion with foreground disk emission, prevent the detection of more than 80% of the clouds (up to 95% during more quiescent phases), while those detected appear less massive, less turbulent and less elongated, with column densities underestimated by a factor of two; only their velocities are reliably recovered. Once these effects are included, the simulated clouds broadly reproduce the properties and sky distribution of the GBT population, but lack the fastest (> 250 km/s ) and highest-latitude (b > 10{\deg} ) clouds. Mock UV absorption and soft X-ray observations support this picture, with warm-ionized gas column densities at the low end of the observed range and X-ray emission measures too low at b > 10{\deg} . Our results imply that the true GC cloud population is more numerous, massive, turbulent and elongated than observed, and that fully reproducing observations may require a stronger recent starburst or additional feedback.

item.title: Chemical abundances of a Galactic Centre ejecta discovered in DESI
item.description: arXiv:2611.02409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chemical abundances in the Galactic Centre (GC) are challenging to measure because of high extinction, crowding, and distance, and are typically limited to the brightest AGB and M giants observed in the near-infrared. In contrast, hypervelocity stars (HVSs) ejected from the GC by Sgr A* carry their natal composition into accessible regions such as the Milky Way halo, making them unique probes of GC chemistry. We present high-resolution optical Magellan/MIKE spectroscopy of DESI-312, a bound HVS candidate in the halo with super-solar metallicity ($[\mathrm{Fe/H}]=0.2\pm0.1$). This sets it apart from accreted halo populations on radial orbits and is most naturally explained by GC formation and Hills-mechanism ejection. Updated isochrone fits give an age of 7.4-11.3 Gyr; together with its metallicity and kinematics, this strengthens the case for a GC origin. Korg and Turbospectrum spectral synthesis yields $[\mathrm{X/Fe}]$ for 22 elements, plus Li from an independent line-by-line NLTE analysis. As DESI-312 is near the main sequence, its C, N, and O abundances are unaltered by dredge-up; to our knowledge, these are the first such measurements of unevolved GC material. Its abundance pattern lies where the nuclear star cluster (NSC), nuclear stellar disc (NSD), and inner-bulge sequences overlap, with a Na enhancement ($[\mathrm{Na/Fe}]=+0.16^{+0.03}_{-0.04}$) more modest than in NSC giants of similar metallicity. Chemistry alone thus cannot identify its progenitor; we nevertheless favour the NSC, given its large reservoir of old, metal-rich stars and the star's kinematics. Alongside WINERED-HVS1 and the S-star S0-6/S10, whose abundances point to different progenitors, this tentatively suggests multiple progenitor populations for the S-star cluster. DESI-312 is a test case for sampling GC chemistry with ejected dwarfs at optical wavelengths, complementing near-infrared studies of giants.

item.title: The Stellar-Mass Dependence of Feedback-Driven Outflows in DESI DR1 Star-Forming Galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2611.02580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stellar feedback plays a key role in regulating star formation and shaping the evolution of star-forming galaxies. Low-mass galaxies provide one of the most powerful laboratories for testing stellar feedback and its impact on galaxy evolution. Numerical simulations predict that repeated feedback-driven gas inflows and outflows generate a "breathing mode," producing a positive correlation between mass-normalized gas velocity dispersion and recent star formation in dwarf galaxies. Whether this kinematic signature persists at higher stellar masses has remained untested. We investigate this question using $\sim1200$ star-forming galaxies with Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectroscopy and COSMOS2020 photometry spanning $7.9<\log M_\star/M_\odot<11.5$ within $z<0.25$. Ionized-gas kinematics are measured with pPXF, and recent star formation histories are reconstructed through joint spectrophotometric fitting with Prospector. We confirm the predicted positive correlation throughout the low-mass regime with $\log M_\star/M_\odot \lesssim 9.8$, quantitatively consistent with previous observations and FIRE-2 simulations. Above $\log M_\star/M_\odot \sim 9.8$, the correlation weakens rapidly and becomes consistent with zero, providing the first empirical constraint on the stellar mass scale above which the kinematic signature of feedback-driven outflow cycles becomes negligible. Our results establish a characteristic stellar mass above which stellar feedback no longer dominates galaxy-scale gas kinematics, providing a new observational benchmark for models of feedback-regulated galaxy evolution. Future joint analyses of gas kinematics and stellar structure will test whether this transition is accompanied by the broader galaxy response predicted by the breathing mode scenario.

item.title: See you again: an $80^\circ$ NGC~5466 stellar stream and its constraints on the Galactic dark halo mass
item.description: arXiv:2611.02653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using \textit{Gaia} Data Release 3 combined with Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Legacy Imaging Survey Data Release 9 and Panoramic Survey Telescope and Rapid Response System Data Release 2, we apply a modified matched filter method to obtain a weighted stellar map in the surrounding of the globular cluster NGC~5466. Our results support that the tidal stream of NGC~5466 extends around $80^\circ$ on the sky, and the leading tail seemingly exhibits an upward deviation in the range of $180^\circ \lesssim \alpha \lesssim 190^\circ$, which supports previous claim that the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) may have caused dynamical perturbations to the stream. Based on the 308 highly-weighted member candidates of the NGC~5466 stream, we try to measure the mass distribution of the Milky Way dark matter halo along with the mass of LMC. By comparing the observed stream candidate members to a series of model streams generated under different potential parameters, we obtain the posterior distributions of the parameters: the circular velocity at the solar radius $V_{\rm c} = 239.56^{+1.46}_{-1.44}\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, the density flattening of the halo $q = 1.08^{+0.07}_{-0.07}$, the scale radius of the halo density profile $r_s = 12.97^{+3.02}_{-2.18}\ \mathrm{kpc}$ and the total mass of the LMC $M_{\rm LMC} = 9.63^{+1.89}_{-2.00}\times 10^{10}$ $\mathrm{M_\odot}$. The enclosed mass of the Milky Way within the stream apocenter radius of $\sim$ 50 kpc is calculated as $M_{\rm MW}(<50~\mathrm{kpc}) = 4.59^{+0.48}_{-0.37} \times 10^{11}$ $\mathrm{M_\odot}$.

item.title: An Empirical Temperature Relation for Chemical Abundances in AGN
item.description: arXiv:2611.02915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present for the very first time the empirical temperature structure of the narrow line region (NLR) clouds of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) based on a sample of [N II] and [O III] auroral line measurements. The scaling of Te([N II]) with Te([O III]), expressed as the t2-t3 relation, is key to deriving accurate chemical abundances, in AGNs and other line-emitting nebulae, particularly when only one auroral line is observed. Here, we provide the first robust empirical description of t2-t3 for AGNs: t2(10^4 K)=1.285*t3(10^4 K)+0.799. We find substantial changes in 12+log(O/H) when compared to other t2-t3 calibrations when using the direct, or Te, method with only the [O III] 4363 auroral line. We find that adopting our t2-t3 most accurately recovers the fully direct method 12+log(O/H). To interpret the physical mechanisms behind the AGN t2-t3, we compare the observed distribution of [N II] 6584/5755 and [O III] 5007/4363 flux ratios to a variety of ionization model predictions. We find evidence for power law density gradients, pressure stratification, and (sometimes significant) contributions from astrophysical shocks driving much of the dispersion on these flux ratios while metal cooling dominates the primary shape of the distribution. With more accurate t2-t3 and 12+log(O/H), the properties of the interstellar medium photoionized by AGN can be better characterized and understood across a wide range of cosmic time and may bring better context for novel observations at z>6 with JWST, with implications for understanding chemical enrichment in the earliest stages of galaxy evolution.

item.title: Kinematic analysis of the TNG50 Milky Way and Andromeda analogues
item.description: arXiv:2611.02920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate whether Ogorodnikov-Milne (O-M) parameters can serve as kinematic tracers of spiral structure in four Milky Way- and Andromeda-like disc galaxies from the TNG50-1 simulation at z=0. Stellar particles are analysed in disc-aligned reference frames, with velocities referenced to the mass-weighted mean stellar velocity within one stellar half-mass radius. Local O-M fits on a regular grid yield centroid velocities and the components of the velocity-gradient tensor, characterising local deformation and rotation. We compare their spatial distributions with stellar surface-density and relative overdensity maps and examine the influence of parameter uncertainties. The galaxies exhibit diverse coherent kinematic patterns. Features selected using the generalised Oort constants A, B, and C+K display partial correspondence with stellar overdensities, depending on the galaxy and the adopted centroid-selection criteria. For TNG50-456326, a galaxy-specific selection enables us to fit four logarithmic spiral branches and determine their geometrical parameters. Their morphology suggests two principal arms and two secondary branches. We compare the fitted spirals with stellar- and gas-mass overdensity and radial velocity maps and examine the spatial relationship between the identified stellar structures and the gas distribution. Qualitative similarities to the morphology and kinematic patterns of the Milky Way make TNG50-456326 a promising candidate for further investigation as a kinematic analogue. Our results support the use of local O-M parameters as complementary diagnostics of non-axisymmetric disc structure, while highlighting the need for galaxy-specific selection criteria.

item.title: J-PAS: Exploring the connection between local environment and the triggering of bursty star formation in Extreme Emission Line Galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2611.02965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: [Abridged]Extreme Emission Line Galaxies (EELGs) are compact, low-mass systems undergoing intense bursts of star formation, whose physical conditions resemble those of galaxies in the early Universe. We characterise the local environment of EELGs identified in the J-PAS survey to determine whether their extreme properties are associated with the presence of nearby companions, as expected if galaxy-galaxy interactions were the main trigger of the burst. We analyse 917 EELGs from the J-PAS internal data release at $0.03 \lesssim z \lesssim 0.9$ over $\sim$30 deg$^2$. We use the Pair Probability Function formalism, based on the full photometric redshift probability distributions, to identify companions within projected separations up to 200 kpc and velocity differences up to 500 km s$^{-1}$. Stellar masses, star formation rates, dust attenuation, and metallicity estimates were derived for the EELGs and their companions through SED fitting with CIGALE, and Monte Carlo simulations were used to correct for projection and completeness effects. The average pair fraction of the EELGs is $f_\mathrm{pair} = 0.162^{+0.048}_{-0.033}$, indicating that only $\sim$16% of the sample has detectable companions, a value lower than the observed average for other star-forming galaxies within the adopted limits. When detected within the sensitivity and stellar-mass completeness limits of J-PAS, companions tend to be more massive and to show higher SED-based metallicity estimates than the EELGs, suggesting that the latter are typically the low-mass components of asymmetric pairs. However, lower-mass companions below these limits may remain undetected. No statistically significant correlation is found between the equivalent widths of the [OIII]$\lambda$5007, H$\beta$, and H$\alpha$ emission lines and the projected separation to the detected companions within the J-PAS limits.

item.title: Decomposition of disk and jet optical emission: Case of PKS~1510-089 and PKS~0736+017
item.description: arXiv:2611.03006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Measuring BLR size and black hole mass of jetted quasars with strong radio emission is challenging due to the contribution from non-thermal synchrotron radiation from the jet in the optical continuum. Here, we investigate the optical continuum emission in two flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs), PKS~0736+017 and PKS~1510-089, by separating the thermal emission from the accretion disk and the non-thermal synchrotron emission from the jet using their distinct polarization signatures. Our analysis combines multi-epoch optical spectro-photometric and polarimetric observations from the archival optical continuum, H$\beta$ emission line light curves from earlier reverberation mapping campaigns, and 37 GHz radio data. For PKS~0736+017, we find that the disk contributes approximately 70 % ($f_d = 0.70^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$) of the total optical emission. After removing the jet component, we obtain a revised H$\beta$ lag of $84.8^{+23.2}_{-18.4}$ days. In contrast, the disk contribution in PKS~1510-089 is lower with 37.5 % ($f_d = 0.37^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$), with a corresponding H$\beta$ lag of $54.4^{+4.4}_{-5.4}$ days. Our findings highlight the need for careful decomposition of optical light curves in jet-dominated AGN.

item.title: What can strong lensing recover in edge-on disc galaxies? A mock study based on TNG50 simulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.03084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong gravitational lensing tightly constrains the projected mass within the Einstein aperture, but what else imaging alone can recover for edge-on disc lenses remains untested against known truth. We construct HST/ACS-like mock observations of 35 edge-on TNG50 disc galaxies selected to resemble lenses from the Sloan WFC Edge-on Late-type Lens Survey (SWELLS), and fit them with a five-stage Source-Light-and-Mass workflow in PyAutoLens; the final model represents the lens mass distribution by scaling the Multi-Gaussian Expansion (MGE) foreground-light template with a global mass-to-light ratio and adding a spherical NFW halo. Decomposed fits succeed for 21 of the 35 systems; in the other 14, coherent MGE lens-light residuals prevent reliable modelling. For the successful subset, the Einstein radius and the total aperture mass are recovered with normalised median absolute deviation (NMAD) scatters of 0.3% and 0.7%. The global projected mass-weighted slope has an NMAD scatter of 10.3%, smaller than that of the mass-sheet-invariant reduced deflection curvature $\xi$ (11.4%) and well below that of the local slope (40.7%), while the stellar and dark-matter aperture masses scatter by 15.1% and 108.8%. A 35-system true-light diagnostic using the exact input light gives component-mass scatters of 0.8% and 6.3%. Under these controlled assumptions, imaging constrains Einstein-scale total mass and global radial structure more reliably than local radial structure or the stellar-dark-matter decomposition.

item.title: GALACTIC CENTERS AS TRACERS OF GALAXY EVOLUTION: Zooming from galaxy large-scale properties into their central massive black holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.03090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: During the workshop ''Galactic Centers as tracers of galaxy evolution'' (Lorentz Center, Leiden), we reviewed one of the most debated questions in the field of galaxy evolution: the connection between galactic central regions and the evolution of galaxies at a global scale. We gathered different research communities to reveal the connection channels between central massive black holes (MBHs), nuclear structures, and evolutionary processes at a global scale, such as gas inflows and outflows and galaxy-galaxy interactions. Special focus was dedicated to MBH seeding, formation and growth, active galactic nuclei feedback, and the formation of nuclear stellar structures, without missing a global perspective. Participants from these different fields introduced us to the state of the art in numerical simulations, as well as cutting-edge observational techniques. In addition to achieving a deep understanding of these topics, we set up plans to exploit future facilities such as the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). In this paper, we briefly summarize the highlights of the workshop, identify the open questions that emerged during the workshop discussions, and discuss what observations and simulations will be needed to address them.

item.title: Molecular gas in the disks and tails of ram pressure stripped Coma galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2611.03131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present new IRAM 30 m observations of CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) emission in five Coma cluster galaxies undergoing ram pressure stripping. Molecular gas is detected in four galaxies, and CO emission is clearly detected in the stripped tails of three, extending up to $\sim50$ kpc from the stellar disks. The molecular gas masses in the tails range from a few $\times10^8\,M_\odot$ and account for up to 10-20% of the molecular gas remaining in the parent disks. Compared with field scaling relations, several galaxies exhibit elevated molecular-to-stellar gas ratios despite being H I deficient. This enhancement persists toward the lower-mass end of our sample, even in the massive Coma cluster environment, consistent with ram-pressure-induced compression of atomic gas and enhanced H I-to-H$_2$ conversion in the disks. At the same time, the total gas fractions of most galaxies remain close to those of field galaxies with similar stellar masses when the molecular gas in the tails is included, indicating that gas removal and phase transformation act simultaneously. We further investigate the relation between molecular and ionized gas by comparing CO and H$\alpha$ emission in the stripped regions. Although CO is preferentially detected in H$\alpha$-bright regions, the increased scatter compared with previous studies suggests the presence of both star-forming and diffuse CO components in the tails. Our results highlight the dual role of ram pressure stripping in dense environments: it efficiently removes gas from galaxies while also promoting molecular gas formation in both the disks and stripped material, thereby shaping short-term star formation in cluster galaxies.

item.title: Statistical Modeling of Foreground Galactic Cirrus for Diffuse Halo Light Measurement
item.description: arXiv:2611.03172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Galactic cirrus, the diffuse Milky Way starlight scattered by interstellar dust, has become a major source of systematic uncertainty in measurements of extragalactic diffuse emission at ultra-low surface brightness levels. Proper modeling and correction of this foreground is crucial to unlock the full potential of next-generation deep imaging surveys for studies of faint diffuse emission such as galactic stellar halos, ultra-diffuse galaxies, and intracluster light (ICL). We develop a statistical approach to reconstruct the 2D distribution of the Galactic cirrus while preserving the underlying diffuse extragalactic emission from stellar halos. We combine the broad dust morphology traced by far-infrared emission with multiscale structural information extracted from the optical images. The method synthesizes plausible cirrus structures through iteratively refining the foreground, the smooth diffuse light model, and the residual sky. The performance is assessed through injection--recovery experiments using Euclid VIS observations of the Abell 2390 cluster, which show substantial improvements in recovered stellar halo photometry, although residual biases depend on the local foreground structure and sky estimation. We apply the method to the central Abell 2390 field to correct for a prominent cirrus complex near its brightest cluster galaxy (BCG), revealing a smoother BCG+ICL distribution with a steeper outer light profile and reduced contamination in the integrated light. Our results demonstrate the potential of statistical modeling of Galactic cirrus to improve diffuse light photometry in deep wide-field imaging surveys.

item.title: A Cepheid-based Distance to the Type 1 Seyfert NGC 3783
item.description: arXiv:2611.03226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a Cepheid-based distance to the Type 1 Seyfert NGC 3783 using the Hubble Space Telescope. Images were obtained over 15 visits using nonredundant time spacing, with ten observations in the F350LP filter and eight observations each in the F555W and F814W filters. We found 1541 unique point sources across all observations, and we fit Cepheid templates to analyze these light curves. From these data, we determined a full sample of seven Cepheid candidates. Of these seven candidates, four are the most convincing and comprise our "strong" sample of Cepheid candidates. We fit the period$-$luminosity relationship to the total sample and to our "strong" sample using the LMC calibration by Riess et al. (2019). Adopting an independent distance constraint to the LMC given by Pietrzynski et al. (2019), and correcting for the potential effects of metallicity, we determine a distance modulus of $\mu = 33.118 \pm 0.154$ mag using our strong sample. This value is formally consistent with the value derived using our full sample and corresponds to a distance of $D = 42.03 \pm 2.98$ Mpc. NGC 3783 is therefore among the farthest galaxies with a Cepheid-based distance measurement.
item.dc:creator: Madison Markham, Misty C. Bentz, Laura Ferrarese, Christopher A. Onken, Marianne Vestergaard

item.title: A Physics Informed Neural Network Approach to Decipher Environmental Confinement of Molecular Clouds in the Third Galactic Quadrant
item.description: arXiv:2611.03450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent high-sensitivity and high-resolution surveys of the Third Galactic Quadrant [$219.75 \leq l \leq 229.75$ and $-5.25 \leq b \leq 5.25$], such as the Milky Way Imaging Scroll Painting ( MWISP) survey, have revealed a significant population of molecular clouds (MCs) that appear virially unbound ($\alpha_{vir} > 2$) according to traditional isolated MC models. However, these apparently unstable cloud structures are actually found long-lived and actively undertaking star formation. This inconsistency presents a Virial Paradox. In the present work, we employ a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to address this discrepancy by re-evaluating the stability of 2,091 MCs . Unlike traditional machine learning, our PINN model embeds the complete Eulerian Virial Theorem including external surface pressure support ($P_{ext}$) directly into the network's loss function. This model autonomously discovers a global Galactic pressure field that scales inversely with vertical height ($|z|$) and Galactocentric radius ($R_{GC}$), consistent with the properties of the Galactic Flare. By incorporating this AI-derived pressure support, we demonstrate a dramatic shift in the stability census: 99.9\% of previously thought unbound clouds are found to be in a state of pressure confined equilibrium ($\alpha_{AI} \leq 2$). Furthermore, we find a robust log-log correlation ($R = 0.64$) between our corrected stability parameter and the star formation rate (SFR). This correlation provides independent physical validation that environmental confinement is a primary regulator of star forming efficiency in the outer Galaxy.
item.dc:creator: Ashok Mondal

item.title: VLITE Observations of the Hubble Ultra Deep Field
item.description: arXiv:2611.03546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present 136 hr of 340 MHz observations of the Hubble Ultra Deep Field (HUDF) conducted with the VLA Low-band Ionosphere and Transient Experiment (VLITE), collected commensally with higher-frequency Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) observations. Our deepest image combines 20 hr of data, covers 4 square degrees, and achieves an angular resolution of 8.8 arcsec x 3.8 arcsec with an rms sensitivity of 158 microJy per beam at the field center. We catalog 671 radio sources detected above 5 sigma significance. Correcting for incompleteness using injection-recovery simulations with a model radio continuum population, we show that our source counts recover the sub-mJy star-forming galaxy population at abundances consistent with other deep fields at comparable frequencies. The data span 45 observing days across two VLA A-configuration semesters separated by 1.3 years, providing a search for variability on ~1-year timescales at sub-mJy flux densities. We identify eleven variable sources with flux densities of 1-100 mJy and modulation indices of 6-40%, six of which exhibit peaked radio spectra consistent with compact AGN. Their variability amplitudes are consistent with refractive interstellar scintillation (RISS) predicted for this line of sight, though three sources with modulation indices exceeding 30% likely require an intrinsic contribution. One source, subsequently confirmed as a compact symmetric object through VLBA follow-up observations, demonstrates the potential of VLITE for identifying populations of young radio AGN through commensal low-frequency variability searches.

item.title: Chemical and dynamical evolution of prestellar cores, the dawn of star and planet formation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Studying prestellar cores is crucial to understanding the formation of stellar and planetary systems. To date, we lack a comprehensive survey of their density and velocity structure at small scales (100-1000 au), the gas ionisation state, their lifetimes, and how these properties are influenced by the environment. A deep study into this critical stage of star formation requires a large single-dish (sub)millimetre telescope like AtLAST.
item.dc:creator: Silvia Spezzano, Elena Redaelli, Paola Caselli, Doris Arzoumanian, Arnaud Belloche, Doug Johnstone, Tony Mroczkowski, \'Alvaro S\'anchez-Monge, Olli Sipil\"a, Sigurd S. Jensen, Izaskun Jim\'enez-Serra

item.title: Episodic Star Formation - II. The Origin of the Fundamental Metallicity Relation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Fundamental Metallicity Relation (FMR) extends the mass-metallicity relation (MZR) by including star formation rate (SFR) as a third parameter. At fixed stellar mass, galaxies with higher SFRs tend to have lower gas-phase metallicities. We investigate the physical origin of the FMR in the context of episodic star formation (Gui et al. 2026, paper I of this series) by tracing the evolution histories of 8,979 central star-forming galaxies selected at $z=0$ in TNG100 back to $z=1$. We find that the overall MZR scatter at $z=0$ ($\sim0.11$ dex) comprises both long-lived differences among galaxies ($\sim0.09$ dex) and temporal fluctuations within individual galaxies ($\sim 0.07$ dex). The galaxy-to-galaxy component shows an anticorrelation between SFR and gas-phase metallicity, as shown by the observed FMR. As for the consequence from temporal fluctuation, we track individual histories and stack the upward and downward SFR phases of a refined sample. Time-shift analysis and stacked histories show a well-behaved sequence in which the cold non-star-forming gas reservoir increases (decreases) first, followed by a decrease (increase) in gas-phase metallicity and then a rise (decline) in SFR. This ordering is consistent with a physical scenario where metal-poor gas first replenishes the cold reservoir and dilutes the gas before SFR rises to the peak, followed by feedback-driven gas heating/removal, resulting in a shift in metallicity from dilution to enrichment as SFR decreases towards the valley. This naturally explains the anticorrelation between the SFR and gas-phase metallicities as indicated by the observed FMR.
item.dc:creator: Xuelun Mei, Dandan Xu, Cheng Li, Yuqian Gui, Haoyi Wang

item.title: Stars Can Quench Superradiance Around Supermassive Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.40895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Light scalar fields trigger an instability around rotating black holes which drives the rapid growth of high-density bound states on astrophysically short timescales---a phenomenon known as black hole superradiance. This process is usually tacitly assumed to happen independent of the local environment. Around supermassive black holes, however, orbiting stars and compact objects act as a perturbation that drains energy from the cloud, potentially preventing its formation altogether. In this work, we quantify under what conditions this happens, focusing on bound-free state transitions. We first compute the rate of energy dissipation due to gravitational interactions, finding that the superradiance growth rate almost always dominates the environmental depletion. The two rates are, however, close enough that the conclusion could be overturned once bound-bound transitions are included. Also, the environment dissipates the cloud faster than gravitational-wave emission, implying that stellar environments must be accounted for in a variety of indirect search strategies. We then investigate the impact of the scalar's quadratic couplings to nucleons and electromagnetism, showing that these interactions can greatly enhance energy dissipation, preventing the cloud's formation. This work highlights the importance of accounting for the local environment in studies of superradiance around intermediate and supermassive black holes.
item.dc:creator: Yu Cheng, Andrea Caputo, Giovanni Maria Tomaselli, Samuel J. Witte

item.title: Hidden Neutrino Active Galaxy Candidates: Prospects for Catalog and Stacking Searches with IceCube, IceCube-Gen2, and KM3NeT
item.description: arXiv:2611.00198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In high-energy neutrino astrophysics, the identification of high-energy neutrino sources is a central goal, and jet-quiet active galactic nuclei (AGNs) have emerged as promising candidates. For this purpose, we present a theory-guided, intrinsic X-ray selected sample of hidden neutrino AGN candidates consisting of $28$ X-ray bright AGNs (X-HiNAC), combining the {\em Swift}/BAT and BASS surveys with dedicated {\em NuSTAR} observations and spectral analyses. We compile their intrinsic X-ray fluxes, spectral properties, luminosity distances, and supermassive black hole masses, to provide a coherent sample for neutrino source searches. The sample is physically motivated but remains model independent given that the neutrino flux is proportional to the intrinsic X-ray flux. Using the magnetically powered corona model, we also demonstrate the prospects for individual-source and stacking searches with IceCube-Gen2 and KM3NeT. We identify promising individual targets and find that stacking the remaining sources, excluding NGC 1068, could yield a $5\sigma$ detection within $\sim 5-15$ years under favorable model assumptions at the current and upcoming neutrino observatories. We highlight systematic uncertainties in the adopted source parameters, particularly the black hole masses, for which different measurement techniques can yield estimates differing by up to an order of magnitude. Such uncertainties can significantly affect the predicted neutrino emission, motivating more precise black hole mass measurements and improved broadband X-ray observations. Our findings motivate improved multiwavelength characterization of nearby AGNs and provide a guide for investigating their role as high-energy neutrino sources.
item.dc:creator: Mainak Mukhopadhyay, Jose Alonso Carpio, Heer Patel, Ali Kheirandish, Kohta Murase

item.title: Intranight optical monitoring of eight quasars with superluminal jets and low optical polarization: Probing the mechanism of rapid flux variability
item.description: arXiv:2611.00207v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Intranight optical variability (INOV) of blazars whose emission arises predominantly from a relativistic jet, has been widely linked to a combination of two key observational diagnostics: the fractional optical polarization ($P_{opt}$) and the Doppler boost arising from relativistic beaming of the jet's emission. To discern which of these two factors plays the dominant role, we investigate INOV of a well-defined representative sample of 8 flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs, which are `low-synchrotron-peaked' blazars) whose jets exhibit a low degree of polarization ($P_{opt}$ < 3$\%$) but a large superluminal motion with c$\beta_{app}$ = 5c $-$ 31c (median = 10c). We report sensitive optical monitoring of these 8 `low-polarization superluminal quasars' (LPSQs) using a 1.3-metre telescope, in 20 sessions of minimum 3-hour duration. These data were supplemented with similarly high-quality monitoring data/results available in the literature for this sample, thus adding another 19 sessions. Duty cycle (DC) of strong INOV (amplitude $\psi > 5\%$) is found to be zero, applying the normally used $F_{\eta}$ test, and $\sim 7\%$ using the more powerful `enhanced $F$-test'. The small DC, despite the strong Doppler boost expected from the observed high superluminality, shows that strong INOV is much rarer among LPSQs, compared to high-polarization quasars, for which DC $(\psi > 5\%$) is found to be around 30%, even using the $F_{\eta}$ test. This provides the first compelling evidence that optical polarization is the primary diagnostic of INOV, while relativistic beaming plays a supportive role. Possible implications for the proposed mechanisms for INOV are pointed out.
item.dc:creator: Krishan Chand, Gopal-Krishna, Ashutosh Tomar, Vibhore Negi, Hum Chand, Suvendu Rakshit

item.title: A VLT/CRIRES+ study of helium 1.083$\mu$m absorption features towards the inner Orion Nebula
item.description: arXiv:2611.00215v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: JWST NIRCam F115W observations towards the inner Orion Nebula revealed a diverse array of previously unknown dark features. The most likely cause was absorption or suppressed emission of the helium 1.083$\mu$m triplet which lies in that filter. We have obtained VLT/CRIRES+ high-resolution spectrographic observations over a selection of different dark targets, confirming that the features are indeed explained by a reduction in the flux of the helium 1.083$\mu$m triplet, a reduction that is fairly uniform across the line. The Orion Nebula is a blister HII region, with a dense, bright ionised layer on the far side from the observer near the Orion A molecular cloud and lower density gas elsewhere. Using a simple radiative transfer model, we show that dark features arise when emission from the dense layer is absorbed by intermediate density helium (e.g. in clumps, globules, or winds from objects like proplyds) on the near side of the dense layer.
item.dc:creator: Thomas J. Haworth, Mark McCaughrean, Mario van den Ancker, James E. Owen, John Bally, Samuel Pearson

item.title: Boosted Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Homogeneous and Non-Homogeneous Lane-Emden Type Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.00701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Lane-Emden Equation is a class of nonlinear differential equations commonly used to model phenomena in astrophysics and mathematical physics, such as stellar structure and thermal behavior in polytropic gas spheres. This study presents a novel hybrid framework that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with boosting methods to enhance the accuracy and robustness of solutions for Lane-Emden type differential equations. Standard PINNs leverage physical laws encoded within the loss function, but their predictive performance can be constrained by optimization challenges and approximation errors. To address this, we introduce a post-processing boosting stage where the residual errors from the PINN prediction are modeled using some regression algorithms - including LightGBM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Regression (SVR). The outputs from these boosted models are aggregated to generate a corrected, high-fidelity prediction. The proposed methodology is systematically validated through quantitative metrics and comparative analysis against the standard PINN baseline. The results demonstrate that the boosted PINN framework significantly reduces prediction error, and improves generalization, offering a powerful and flexible approach for solving scientific and engineering problems governed by differential equations.
item.dc:creator: Luke Oluwaseye Joel

item.title: Tracking the evolution of sub-Neptunes. I. Gyrochronology of planet hosting stars
item.description: arXiv:2611.00856v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stellar age is fundamental for reconstructing planetary-system evolution but remains difficult to determine for unevolved main-sequence stars. Stellar rotation provides a sensitive age diagnostic and a temporal framework for investigating the evolution of close-in planets. This is the first paper in a series aimed at tracing the evolution of the sub-Neptune population through homogeneous ages of their host stars. We compiled rotation periods and stellar parameters for 4639 confirmed exoplanet hosts. Gyrochronological ages were inferred using a two-zone rotational evolution model and a Bayesian approach combining rotation periods, dereddened Gaia (BP-RP) colours, and literature stellar masses as Gaussian priors. Rotational tracks were extended to the terminal-age main sequence, beyond the empirical calibration range. We obtain gyrochronological constraints for 2204 host stars. Well-constrained ages have typical formal uncertainties of 10--15%, offering substantially greater precision than is generally achievable through isochrone fitting for unevolved stars. Inferred stellar masses agree with the literature priors, while model effective temperatures are consistent with independent determinations. Ages beyond the open-cluster calibration range remain model-dependent. The resulting homogeneous catalogue provides the age framework for investigating the evolution of sub-Neptune populations and the emergence of the radius valley. Stellar parameters, provenance, and gyrochronological results are publicly available through CDS.

item.title: Harmonic Angular Mapping Method for Binary Microlensing Grid Search
item.description: arXiv:2611.02326v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Searching for binary-lens microlensing solutions is computationally demanding because of the complex parameter space and the large number of trial models required. We present an algorithm that accelerates binary-lens grid searches by expanding the angular dependence of precomputed magnification maps in Fourier modes. By contracting the observation-dependent weighted sums in Fourier space, the $\chi^2$ values for all trial source-trajectory angles can be evaluated efficiently using inverse fast Fourier transforms (FFTs), avoiding repeated calculations over individual observations. We tested the method on 200 Roman-like synthetic binary-lens events. For 166 events (83%), the recovered fits agreed with Levenberg--Marquardt fits initialized at the injected parameters to within $|\Delta\chi^2|\leq1$. The FFT map scan required an average of 5.05~min per event. For the same discrete search volume, the Fourier angular evaluation was estimated to be approximately 900 times faster than conventional magnification-map sampling. These results demonstrate that the method can efficiently identify useful initial conditions for binary-lens light-curve modeling.
item.dc:creator: Kansuke Nunota

item.title: An all-sky catalogue of Be transition stars from WISE and Gaia
item.description: arXiv:2611.02450v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an all-sky catalogue of classical Be stars undergoing transitions between quiescent B-type and active Be-star phases, based on Gaia DR3 astrometry and multi-epoch mid-infrared photometry from WISE and NEOWISE-R. From a Gaia-selected parent sample of 4.2 million candidate OBA stars, we identify Be transition stars through correlated variability in $W_1$ magnitude and $W_1-W_2$ colour, which traces circumstellar disk formation and dissipation. The final catalogue contains 3,300 Be transition stars, including 2,743 newly identified objects, and provides a large, homogeneous sample for studying Be outburst activity across the sky. The median durations of the measured outburst and decay phases are 459 and 478 days, respectively, consistent with previous WISE-based measurements and compatible with the long disk-evolution timescales expected in the viscous decretion disk framework. As an initial application, we use TESS photometry for 3,017 targets to identify 63 eclipsing binary systems hosting Be transition stars, including 33 Algol-type, 17 Beta Lyrae-type, and 13 W Ursae Majoris-type systems. Among the multi-epoch LAMOST spectra, two sources show candidate radial-velocity shifts exceeding 20 km s $^{-1}$; their line-profile behaviour suggests that RV variability in active Be transition stars may be influenced by outburst-related line-profile changes rather than being an unambiguous indicator of binary motion. This catalogue provides a basis for future statistical studies of Be outbursts, disk evolution, and their connection with binarity and spectroscopic variability.
item.dc:creator: Qi Jia, Mingjie Jian, Gang Li, Qian Cui, Chengyuan Li

item.title: Two Fast Radio Burst Candidates Detected in the RATAN-600 Blind Survey
item.description: arXiv:2611.02697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report the detection of two single dispersed pulses with widths of about 6.7\,ms and 15.6\,ms and flux densities of about 0.8 and 1.7\,Jy. These were found in a blind survey of two circular regions (Dec$\;=+22^{\circ}$ and $+5^{\circ}$,RA: 0--24~h) at high radio frequencies \mbox{(4400--5000\,MHz)} using four 4-channel filter radiometers (central frequencies of 4475, 4625, 4775, and 4925\,MHz) spanning a total frequency bandwidth of 600\,MHz. The survey was carried out with the Western Sector antenna of the RATAN-600 radio telescope, which had an effective area of 1200\,m$^2$ in~2017--2025. The total area of the survey was about 1500~square degrees, and each pointing of the antenna lasted one year. We consider these to be two rare, high-frequency FRB events (MJD~58614.38257 and MJD~58659.62482), detected with estimated dispersion measures of $200\pm20$ and $266\pm10$\,pc\,cm$^{-3}$ at a final signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) level of 8--9 after additional optimal filtration. After subtraction of the estimated dispersions within the Milky Way, we estimated redshifts of approximately 0.09 and 0.13, respectively, using the traditional equation: ${\rm DM}\,[{\rm pc~cm}^{-3}] = 1000\,z$ for the intergalactic medium. The estimated isotropic energies of the FRBs are equal to $10^{40}$\,erg and $2\times 10^{40}$\,erg, respectively. To effectively detect single pulses, we applied machine learning methods using a neural network trained on synthetic FRB pulse profiles.

item.title: Stellar wind variability in OB stars and its effect on mass-loss determinations
item.description: arXiv:2611.03363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Virtually all stellar winds of OB stars exhibit variability in one spectral diagnostic or another. This review focuses primarily on UV spectroscopic signatures of this variability and on studies that have exploited it to reveal the presence of large-scale velocity and density structures in the winds. The review includes demonstrations that the physical structures responsible for the variations appear to be large, spatially coherent and rooted in the stellar photospheres. Furthermore, evidence is summarised that these structures can be optically thick to resonance line radiation and are dense enough to modulate the X-ray fluxes that originate in the wind. Also discussed, is how the structures can affect wind line formation and, as a result, the precision by which mass-loss rates can be determined. The potential of millimetre and radio continuum observations to constrain the radial stratification of wind clumping is highlighted, as a future path to reliable empirical determinations of massive star mass-loss rates.
item.dc:creator: Raman K. Prinja

item.title: Episodic Protostellar Outflows: A Proper Motion Study in Serpens South
item.description: arXiv:2611.03559v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Serpens South is a notable protostellar cluster with signatures of recent star formation, including a high protostellar fraction. Within the region, several protostars provide important mechanical feedback via outflows. We investigate the molecular outflow driven by the Class 0 protostar known as CARMA-7, which is located in the central hub of Serpens South. Two epochs of observations with the Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) with sub-arcsecond resolution capture the well-collimated, episodic outflow with distinct ejecta knots. This outflow, traced with 12CO J = 3-2 and SiO J = 8-7, appears to be mostly blueshifted to the south and redshifted to the north, with radial velocities up to at least 25 km/s. We present the first proper motion study of this outflow by comparing observations taken in 2017 and 2021. The measured proper motions trace the ejection history and refine the inferred outflow morphology. We find that proper motions of the 12CO J = 3-2 and SiO J = 8-7 knots range between 10 - 40 mas/yr, corresponding to 30-90 km/s. Using radial velocities and proper motions, we determined that the inclinations of the outflow lobes are ~60 -80 degrees relative to the line of sight. Finally, we measure ejection timescales as recent as ~10 to ~120 years, and we discuss this in the context of other known protostars with recent ejecta events.

item.title: A JWST MIRI LRS Survey of 37 Massive Star-Forming Galaxies and AGN at Cosmic Noon -- Overview and First Results
item.description: arXiv:2510.07365v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a large spectroscopic survey with JWST's Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) Low Resolution Spectrometer (LRS) targeting $37$ infrared-bright galaxies between $z=0.65-2.46$ with infrared luminosities $\log L_{\rm IR}/L_\odot>11.5$ and $\log M_*/M_\odot=10-11.5$. Targets were taken from a Spitzer $24\,\mu$m-selected sample with archival spectroscopy from the Infrared Spectrograph (IRS) and include a mix of star-forming galaxies and dust-obscured AGN. By combining IRS with the increased sensitivity of LRS, we expand the range of spectral features observed between $5-30\,\mu$m for every galaxy in our sample. In this paper, we outline the sample selection, JWST data reduction, 1D spectral extraction, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) feature measurements from $\lambda_{rest}=3.3-11.2\,\mu$m. In the \textit{JWST} spectra, we detect PAH emission features at $3.3-5.3\,\mu$m, as well as Paschen and Brackett lines. The $3.3\,\mu$m feature can be as bright as $1\%$ of the $8-1000\,\mu$m infrared luminosity and exhibits a tight correlation with the dust-obscured star-formation rate. We detect absorption features from CO gas, CO$_2$ ice, H$_2$O ice, and aliphatic dust. From the joint JWST and Spitzer analysis we find that the $11.3/3.3\,\mu$m PAH ratios are on-average three times higher than that of local luminous, infrared galaxies. This is interpreted as evidence that the PAH grains are larger at $z\sim1-2$. The size distribution may be affected by coagulation of grains due to high gas densities and low temperatures. These conditions are supported by the observation of strong water ice absorption at $3.05\,\mu$m, and can lower stellar radiative feedback as large PAHs transmit less energy per photon into the interstellar medium.

item.title: The inner dark-matter structure of TNG50 simulated galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2604.02566v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the $\Lambda$CDM framework, galaxies evolve within dark matter (DM) haloes, where baryonic processes can modify the inner structure of the DM distribution. In particular, the condensation of baryons and associated feedback mechanisms can alter the inner density profiles of haloes, motivating detailed studies of their central regions. We investigate inner DM density slopes in TNG50 galaxies, their relation to galaxy properties, and their cosmic evolution. We assess baryonic effects on the inner DM structure by comparing galaxies with their DM-only (DMO) counterparts. We constructed spherically averaged DM density profiles in both runs. The inner slope was quantified using an inner linear fit, defined as a direct power-law fit to the central region of the density profiles and motivated by the asymptotic behaviour of generalised Navarro-Frenk-White models. Subhaloes were matched between simulations and tracked across redshifts $z = 0$, $0.2$, $0.7$, and $1$. The inner DM structure of galaxies in TNG50 shows that high-stellar-mass systems ($M_\star \gtrsim 10^{11}$ M$_\odot$) exhibit shallow inner slopes regardless of whether they are centrals or satellites, while lower-mass galaxies ($M_\star \lesssim 10^9$ M$_\odot$) show a broader diversity of profiles. At fixed stellar mass, low-mass satellites tend to be more cuspy, with the steepest slopes found in redder systems with lower $V_{\mathrm{max}}$ in more massive host haloes. At the population level, we find a modest cosmic evolution, with steeper profiles towards low redshifts in the hydrodynamical run and the opposite trend in DMO, while hydrodynamical galaxies remain systematically steeper at all redshifts. Finally, we verified that the fiducial interval provides the most suitable reference for measuring the shallowest inner slopes of DM density profiles at the TNG50 resolution limit.
